claims.object_text: transmembrane protein and member of the protocadherin family
claims.quote: PCDH19 is a transmembrane protein and member of the protocadherin family.
more than 200 mutations have been linked to the neurodevelopmental PCDH-clustering epilepsy (PCDH19-CE) syndrome.

claims.object_text: mosaic absence of PCDH19 causes disturbed cell-cell contact proposed to cause the syndrome
claims.quote: A disturbed cell-cell contact that arises when random X-inactivation creates mosaic absence of PCDH19 has been proposed to cause the syndrome.

claims.object_text: roles in neuronal proliferation, migration, and synapse function
claims.quote: Several studies have shown roles for PCDH19 in neuronal proliferation, migration, and synapse function, yet most of them have focused on cortical and hippocampal neurons.

claims.object_text: cortical interneuron migration is affected by altering PCDH19 dosage
claims.quote: cortical interneuron migration is affected by altering PCDH19 dosage by means of overexpression in brain slices and medial ganglionic eminence (MGE) explants.

claims.object_text: reduced PCDH19 expression causes subtle defects in MGE explants
claims.quote: We also detect subtle defects when PCDH19 expression was reduced in MGE explants, suggesting that the dosage of PCDH19 is important for proper interneuron migration.

claims.object_text: heterozygote, but not in homozygote PCDH19 knockout animals
claims.quote: We confirm this finding in vivo by showing a mild reduction in interneuron migration in heterozygote, but not in homozygote PCDH19 knockout animals.

claims.object_text: subdomains of PCDH19 have a different impact on cell survival and interneuron migration
claims.quote: In addition, we provide evidence that subdomains of PCDH19 have a different impact on cell survival and interneuron migration.

claims.object_text: non-cell-autonomous effect of PCDH19 dosage changes on migration
claims.quote: demonstrating a non-cell-autonomous effect of PCDH19 dosage changes.

claims.object_text: new roles for the extracellular and cytoplasmic domains of PCDH19
claims.quote: Overall, our findings suggest new roles for the extracellular and cytoplasmic domains of PCDH19 and support that cortical interneuron migration is dependent on balanced PCDH19 dosage.
